results.title: Best SSD for Gaming in 2026: NVMe and SATA Picks by Budget | MaxMyBuild
results.content: The best SSD for most gaming builds in 2026 is the Kingston NV3 1TB (around $155 on Amazon): PCIe Gen4, 6,000 MB/s reads, and the lowest price among reliable NVMe drives in this guide. For those willing to spend $20 more, the Crucial P310 1TB ($175) hits 7,100 MB/s — right at the practical speed ceiling where gaming load times stop improving meaningfully. For 2TB, the Crucial T700 2TB with heatsink ($235) is the standout pick: PCIe Gen5 speeds at a price that beats most Gen4 2TB drives. [...] The Crucial BX500 is available in 1TB ($175) and 2TB ($247) in 2.5-inch form factor. QLC NAND (Quad-Level Cell, a higher-density NAND type with lower write endurance than TLC), 540/500 MB/s. No cache. [...] To put the value in context: the WD Black SN7100 2TB costs $295 with Gen4 speeds of 7,250/6,900 MB/s. The T700 2TB with heatsink costs $60 less for Gen5 speeds that are 70% higher. This pricing gap is real: the T700 launched in 2023 and prices have dropped substantially since then, while the SN7100 is a 2025 drive still at launch pricing. The 4GB DRAM buffer means sustained write performance holds up better than any other drive in this guide.

results.title: SSD Price Trend 2026: 1TB and 2TB NVMe Buying Outlook
results.content: The reason is NAND supply. TrendForce reported on March 31, 2026 that NAND Flash contract prices were projected to rise sharply in 2Q26, driven by AI server and data center demand. TrendForce also noted that NAND capacity is increasingly being allocated to enterprise SSDs, while consumer applications scale back under cost pressure. That matters for ordinary 1TB and 2TB NVMe buyers because consumer SSD pricing does not move in isolation. [...] TrendForce’s NAND Flash price page listed 1Q26 PC-client OEM SSD contract prices for value-grade PCIe TLC drives, including a 1TB mSATA/M.2 TLC PCIe value-grade average of 153.90 and a 512GB average of 97.10. These are contract-market snapshots, not universal online retail prices, but they are useful because they show the cost base that many downstream SSD quotes sit on top of. [...] Updated August 5, 2026. Halfway through the year, the 2026 price story has two chapters. Contract prices surged more than 100% across the first half, with the steepest quarter-on-quarter jumps landing in Q2. Now the curve is bending: TrendForce projects NAND contract prices to rise a further 10–15% in Q3 — still up, but no longer runaway.
